key_insight: PC-GNO learns the full mid-plane six-component stress tensor field in concrete penetration by coupling graph message passing with physics-informed impedance-based interactions and spectral normalization.
engineering_relevance: This enables surrogate prediction of field-level impact response from design inputs alone, supporting faster penetration-resistant concrete assessment than aggregate-resolved FEM.
method: Train on 359 full-scale, aggregate-resolved FEM cases at 100, 135, and 165 m/s across 14, 23, and 48 MPa concrete strengths.
Build graph coupling strength from material impedance contrast across interfaces.
Predict the complete six-component tensor field in function space rather than a single scalar response.
evidence_signal: The model was verified against laboratory measurements and achieved mean accuracy of 80.16% across the three levels, outperforming the preceding-frame field baseline and a linear regression benchmark.
watch_item: Performance is tied to the training/evaluation conditions, so generalization to other projectile types, geometries, or concrete mixes may require retraining or validation.
paper_title: A physics-coupled graph neural operator for mid-plane six-component stress tensor field prediction in concrete penetration
